perf_self_review.method: Exact period-weighted direct sampled-IP attribution from perf report --no-children --call-graph none; no caller or inclusive cost inferred.
perf_self_review.scope: Whole-process user-cycle samples, including launcher/startup, corpus and oracle work, setup, timer-excluded checks, destruction and reporting; not operation-exclusive.
limits: Use period weights rather than sample counts; the reducer reconciles flat report periods to raw leaf samples and the header total.
Keep unresolved sampled IPs separate and do not interpret them as kernel or application work.
DWARF stacks are too incomplete for caller, ancestry or inclusive attribution; the runner's small self row is not a total runner-cost estimate.
Resolved symbols are whole-process hotspot observations, not timer-exclusive scan costs or optimization proof.

callgrind_review.scope: Two separately captured 10-sample/zero-warmup guest-instruction diagnostics for the toggle function, including oracle/setup and timer-excluded work; not exact timer scope.
limits: Inclusive rows overlap; mce_start is inside MCE processing and rows must not be summed.
Ir counts are Valgrind-instrumented guest instructions and cannot be compared with native cycle periods, wall time, allocation cost or speedup.
The brk segment overflow warning is retained as an environment limitation.
The child diagnostic echo is not a second run: totals are read from the final raw file whose parent PID is recorded above.
The timed closure in run_xlsx_full_cell_scan is inlined in the retained binary, so exact timer-only Callgrind attribution would require a rebuild or an in-code client marker.

source_scope.oracle_before_timer: full_cell_scan_oracle and source/archive identity setup occur before the iteration loop; source and scanner setup then occur before each iteration's clock.
source_scope.timed_region: SourceBackedWorkbook::from_read_at, sheet enumeration, and all sheet cell visits through the scanner callback.
source_scope.after_timer: source-version/tolerance checks, digest/count/oracle checks, observation recording, drops and result handling.
